newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Intel CFO sees higher Q4 growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Intel CFO sees higher Q4 growth.

text.p: Intel Corp's chief financial officer said the chip giant is getting especially strong orders for high performance microprocessors amid "healthy" demand for its chips generally.

The demand for its Pentium Pro and high-end Pentium microprocessors -- the chips that power personal computers -- are a big part of why Intel expects its revenue and gross margin to grow "significantly" in the fourth quarter from the third quarter, CFO Andy Bryant said in an interview.
Demand is so strong that personal computer makers are ordering chips several months in advance of what they need, something they haven't done all year.
"Customers are booking for longer periods of time," Bryant said, describing the booking periods as several months instead of a few weeks, as had been the case for most of this year.

Bryant indicated that Intel expects the revenue jump between the third and fourth quarter to be greater than the 11 percent revenue jump between the second and third quarter because, "for the last five years, our fourth quarter revenue growth rate was greater than third quarter rates."

Bryant was interviewed on Wednesday after Intel ended its silence on the future that it started in September because of a California ballot initiative that would have put severe liabilities on company officers and directors regarding shareholders expectations. The initiative was defeated on November 5.
"We see a healthy environment for our products at this time" from all parts of the world, Bryant said.
Industry watchers have speculated that demand for Pentium Pros and Pentiums is strong enough that supplies are tight.
"We believe we can meet our customers' demands at this time, but it's a careful balancing act between customer demand and what our factories can produce," Bryant said."

Analyst Dan Kleskin of Robertson, Stephens & Co said the demand comes from corporations ungrading their PCs to Pentium Pros as well as from PC makers expecting strong consumer demand for the holiday season.
Intel Corp. is the world's largest semiconductor maker.
